newsitem.title: USA: New England Electric in $1.59 billion deal with PG&E.
newsitem.headline: New England Electric in $1.59 billion deal with PG&E.

text.p: New England Electric System said Wednesday it agreed to sell its non-nuclear generating business to an affiliate of PG&E Corp. for $1.59 billion in cash.
The deal would result in an average price drop of about 15 percent for New England Electric's 1.3 million customers, the utility said.
In anticipation of the proceeds from the deal, New England Electric said it also authorised the repurchase of up to 5 million of its common shares.
Westborough, Mass.-based New England Electric is a $2.3 billion, public utility holding company. Its retail and wholesale power units supply customers in Massachusetts and Rhode Island.
San Francisco-based PG&E provides energy services throughout North America and Australia.

The agreement calls for New England Electric's New England Power Co. and Narragansett Electric Co. subsidiaries to sell 18 power plants and 23 power contract obligations to PG&E affiliate U.S. Generating Co. The deal would reduce New England Electric's "stranded investment," paying off nearly all of its fossil, hydro and nuclear power plant investments, the company said.

The $1.59 billion includes $225 million to be paid when customer choice of power supplier becomes widely available in New England. That amount begins to decline if choice is not available by Jan. 1, 1999.

New England Power said it would pay between $150 million and $170 million annually through January 2008 to offset the above-market portion of power purchase contracts assumed by U.S. Generating. New England Electric and its units also would receive $85 million to cover costs from early retirement, special severance and re-training programmes for employees affected by restructuring in the utility industry.
The deal must be approved by state and federal regulators, with decisions expected in 1998, the company said.
New England Electric's stock closed Tuesday at $37 and PG&E ended at $24.31, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
